title: Latency Cartographer: tiling p50/p95/p99 by model family, route and IO-mode
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a reusable Latency Cartographer dashboard that tiles p50/p95/p99 across model families, API routes, and IO-mode (streaming vs non-streaming). The dashboard should enable on-call and SREs to rapidly identify regressions by model family and route, compare streaming vs non-streaming behaviour, and link directly to traces and raw logs for root cause work.

Scope and deliverables:
- Telemetry schema changes: add 'io_mode' tag (values: streaming, nonstreaming), 'model_family' label, and consistent 'servepath' dimension to all derived latency metrics. Instrument the request router and servepath join points with tracing hooks that emit these tags.
- Metrics: emit hdr histogram-backed metrics for request_latency_ms with percentiles and bucketed histograms, and summary metrics for p50/p95/p99 to avoid on-the-fly aggregation costs in dashboards.
- Log pipeline: enrich request logs in Fluentd pipeline to include io_mode and model_family; add a lightweight sampling rule for full KV-cache and kernel selection metadata for 1% of requests to keep payload size reasonable.
- Dashboard: new "Latency Cartographer" board with the following tiles: global overview (p50/p95/p99), route grid (rows=model_family, cols=route) with streaming/non-streaming split per cell, time series sparklines, sided-by-side percentile heatmap for quick hotspots, and trace-explorer links (query params attached).
- Alerts: create advisory SLO alert (p95 > 800ms for any route-model_family-io_mode for >5m) and an urgent alert if p99 > 2s for >3m. Alerts should include a link back to the dashboard and the sample traces.

Acceptance criteria:
- Dashboard surfaces p50/p95/p99 for all model families and top 30 production routes, broken out by io_mode.
- Each cell in grid links to 5 sample traces and the underlying logs for that cohort.
- On-call runbook describes playbook steps and known mitigations (e.g., route fallback to smaller model variant).
- Automated tests validating telemetry tags and enrichment added to CI for telemetry service.

Trade-offs and decisions:
- We will emit p50/p95/p99 as discrete metrics to avoid expensive percentile-by-query at dashboard render time. This increases cardinality but keeps dashboards fast. We scoped to top 30 routes to limit combinatorial explosion across model families.
- Sampling full kernel selection and KV-cache metadata to 1% balances debugging needs vs storage and privacy constraints.

Instrumentation tasks (owners):
- Router tracing hook: Marco (this ticket) — add io_mode header detection and annotate span with servepath and model_family.
- Runtime exporter: Priya — include histogram and compute p50/p95/p99 at scrape time and expose as metrics.
- Logs pipeline: Rafael — add enrichment and sampling rules in Fluentd; update index templates.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature flag telemetry changes behind `latency_cartographer_v1` and enable on staging.
2) Validate metrics and dashboard templates on staging with synthetic traffic.
3) Canary enable on 5% of production traffic for 48 hours and monitor ingestion cost.
4) Full enable after observability cost review and SRE sign-off.

Notes and references:
- Confluence design spec: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OBS/pages/Latency+Cartographer+Design
- Draft dashboard JSON: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ExampleCartographerDraft
- Telemetry PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/348
- Fluentd rules PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform-ops/pull/672

Risks:
- Cardinality explosion if we include too many model_family variants. Mitigation: cap to top model_families by usage and normalize family tags.
- Query costs for on-demand percentile calculation. Mitigation: precompute percentiles and use heatmap tiling to limit queries.

Next steps:
- Marco to push initial tracing hook patch and telemetry PR by 2026-03-18.
- Dashboard JSON skeleton due 2026-03-22.
- Canary and cost review 2026-03-25 to 2026-03-29.
